builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SoU-RHS: Bayesian Structured Sparsity for Compact Architecture Recovery in CNNs
summary: The method replaces deterministic structured-sparsity pruning (and manual width selection) of CNNs with a Bayesian Regularized Horseshoe procedure augmented by a sparse global-local mechanism that recovers a compact filter architecture from an overparameterized reference model. The cost is added training complexity: Bayesian inference over sparsity parameters is slower and more intricate than standard fine-tuning, and implementation effort is nontrivial. It can fail if the recovered layer-wise allocation does not transfer to the reader's task, if pruning thresholds are poorly chosen outside the studied range, or if accuracy losses exceed what the paper's benchmarks suggest on different data.
rationale: Structured filter pruning with a Bayesian sparsity prior is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU and can reduce deployment cost, but its stability and calibration benefits must be validated on the reader's own models and datasets before production adoption.
technique: Bayesian structured sparsity for CNN filter pruning

claims.statement: The method replaces deterministic structured-sparsity pruning (and manual width selection) of CNNs with a Bayesian Regularized Horseshoe procedure augmented by a sparse global-local mechanism that recovers a compact filter architecture from an overparameterized reference model. The cost is added training complexity: Bayesian inference over sparsity parameters is slower and more intricate than standard fine-tuning, and implementation effort is nontrivial. It can fail if the recovered layer-wise allocation does not transfer to the reader's task, if pruning thresholds are poorly chosen outside the studied range, or if accuracy losses exceed what the paper's benchmarks suggest on different data.

Recovers substantially smaller CNN architectures than deterministic structured-sparsity baselines at competitive accuracy, with lower NLL in every evaluated configuration and generally lower ECE; no multiplicative factor reported.
